messages:
Sasha: Heads up — we're planning to deprecate the 'orgless' API key fallback that allowed projectless calls. RFC follow-up: remove in ~8 weeks. Primary reasons: expanded leak surface and big complexity in RBAC and audits.
Matt: Did we quantify customer impact? Any active keys that will break?
Nguyen: Telemetry shows ~1.3% of active keys still hit the orgless shim. Mostly internal infra jobs and a handful of third-party connectors.
Eva: Concern — some background workers use service account keys pinned to project 0. What's the migration story for them?
Ralph: Proposal: two-phase deprecation. Phase 1: soft-deny with warning header `X-Redwood-Warn: orgless-key-deprecating` and verbose audit entries. Phase 2: enforce block after 8 weeks. Provide an autofix tool to reassign keys to a tenant/project.
Matt: +1 to phased approach. Also: surface affected keys in Console and add an export CSV for customers. For Dedicated customers we may need a transient fallback mode behind a support opt-out.
Sasha: Agreed — Dedicated/private customers can request an opt-out but it must be tracked via ticket and limited. We don't want permanent exceptions.
Nguyen: Implementation idea for runtime: middleware checks claim; if org missing -> emit `X-RW-Deprecation: orgless-key` and continue for phase 1, but log metric `auth.orgless_key.count`. Phase 2 flips to 403 with a specific error code.
Eva: RBAC mapping question: previously orgless keys had a loose "service:global" role. We need mapping rules: either map to `org-admin` or `project-service` based on owner-email claim, or force manual reassignment. Automatic mapping risks privilege changes.
Ralph: We can add introspection endpoint to make migration easier: `POST /v1/introspect { key: "..." }` returns claims + recommended target (best-effort). Example CLI: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://auth.redwood.internal/v1/introspect`
infra-bot: deploy status — canary rollout started for compatibility middleware on eng-runtime at 1781123500, 5% hosts.
Matt: What about agent-to-agent delegation patterns? Some connectors proxy requests and rely on orgless semantics. We need a policy for propagating `actor` claims and a recommended pattern for connector owners.
Sasha: Migration plan (short): 1) Announcement + docs + FAQ. 2) Console surface listing affected keys + export. 3) Provide CLI/autofix and introspection. 4) Soft deny with header + telemetry. 5) Full block + limited opt-outs. 6) Post-mortem and lessons. ETA: rollout finish ~8 weeks.
Nguyen: I'll coordinate with Customer Success to reach out to the top 20 tenants that will be impacted.
Eva: We should also update SDKs to surface the deprecation header and give example migration code. Add E2E test harness replaying real traffic to catch edge cases.
Ralph: Telemetry note: tag events with `deprecated_key=true` and include `recommended_target_project` when available. Also increment alerting if rate of `orgless_key` traffic doesn't decline after week 2.
Matt: SGTM. I'll open the deprecation PR with middleware, console changes, and the migration scripts. Will include migration playbook for customers.
Sasha: No objections from me. @Matt please include changelog and rollout runbook. :thumbsup:
